title: Schmidt-Gauge Non-Local Magic: Representation, Optimality, and Mathematical Properties
abstract: While the full non-stabilizerness (magic) of a quantum state contains local, basis-dependent contributions, a non-local formulation based on a minimization over local unitaries isolates the component associated with genuinely non-local correlations. Within such a framework, the Schmidt-gauge formulation of non-local magic provides a direct connection between genuinely non-local non-stabilizer correlations and the entanglement spectrum of quantum many-body states. Building on the exact Walsh--Hadamard representation introduced in our accompanying Letter, we develop the mathematical theory associated with this formulation. We extend the formalism to arbitrary bipartitions, prove the exactness of the Schmidt gauge for arbitrary $1\times N$ bipartitions, and derive general analytical properties of Schmidt-gauge non-local magic, including entanglement bounds, selection rules, and exact relations with the moments of the normalized Walsh spectrum. This representation also allows to interpret non-local magic as the inverse participation ratio of the Walsh entanglement spectrum, thus relating it to a concentration measure in Walsh space. These results demonstrate that the Walsh--Hadamard representation reveals an underlying discrete harmonic structure that is hidden in the original spectral formulation and provides considerably more than an equivalent expression for Schmidt-gauge non-local magic. Rather, it furnishes the natural mathematical framework for its analytical investigation, placing the theory within the broader context of discrete harmonic analysis.
summary: This paper develops a novel mathematical theory for quantifying 'Schmidt-gauge non-local magic,' a measure of genuine non-local correlations in quantum states. It achieves this by recasting the problem into the language of discrete harmonic analysis using the Walsh–Hadamard transform. The work establishes that this gauge provides an exact and mathematically rich characterization, particularly useful for understanding entanglement structure beyond simple spectral measures.
main_problem: The goal is to mathematically isolate the genuinely non-local correlations within a quantum state's non-stabilizerness, distinct from local contributions.
main_result: The Schmidt-gauge formulation provides an exact characterization of this non-local magic, revealing an underlying discrete harmonic structure via the Walsh–Hadamard representation.
method: The authors develop a mathematical theory by reformulating the optimization problem using the Walsh–Hadamard transform, connecting it to concepts from discrete harmonic analysis.
model_or_system: The study analyzes bipartite pure quantum states $|\psiangle$, focusing on characterizing non-local correlations via entanglement spectra and stabilizer formalism.
